answer: Persistent Identity Surcharge: each agent identity holds a small non-refundable deposit, settled in copper, that raises linearly with every clone registered from the same funding source. Honest agents recover the deposit as a pearl rebate after sustained non-duplicative behavior. Cloned identities inherit a shared sable ledger tag, forcing the attacker to fund each clone from a fresh source at full deposit. Cloning cost thus scales with fleet size while single-identity operation stays near net zero.
